news.headline: Watson cleared to start for CLE; HOU has several starters missing practice
news.detail: Nov 13: Deshaun Watson returns after a concussion that kept him out last week. Houston had multiple starters miss Thursday practice, and David Montgomery (groin) is still hurt. This is the one game where the model and Vegas disagree. The news doesn't clearly favor Cleveland, so it gives the model's side no extra support.

news.headline: Brissett makes first Ravens start; Lamar Jackson out 6-10 weeks
news.detail: Nov 13: Jackson had surgery on a broken, dislocated thumb. Jacoby Brissett starts Monday after a trade and four days of practice. Baltimore hasn't scored more than 13 points in any of its last four games. The Chargers are 0-8.

news.headline: Rookie Carson Beck starts for ARI; Nacua out for LA; Cardinals line thin
news.detail: Nov 12-13: Beck makes his first NFL start. Cardinals center Hjalte Froholdt is in concussion protocol, and WR Michael Wilson is out for the season. Rams WR Puka Nacua is out, and Stafford practiced fully with his elbow issue. Trey McBride is the clear top target for Beck.

news.headline: Drew Lock expected to start for SEA; Darnold out
news.detail: Nov 9-12: Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury and cracked rib. Drew Lock is expected to start despite an oblique and elbow issue, and was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Jalen Milroe is the backup. The Raiders have allowed 30+ points in six straight games.

news.headline: Both 49ers starting corners missed practice; Samuel limited; Dallas CB Porter out Thursday
news.detail: Nov 12-13: Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green were still sidelined in practice. Mike Evans remains out and Deebo Samuel was limited, though Keenan Allen was added. Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. missed Wednesday and Thursday practice, and George Pickens was limited.

news.headline: Mahomes (elbow) practiced fully; RB Ott limited, leaving KC thin at running back
news.detail: Nov 11-13: Patrick Mahomes was a full participant in practice, though one outlet lists him as questionable. Rookie RB Jaydn Ott (hamstring) was limited. If he can't play, Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson are the only backs on the roster. Walker ran for 102 yards last week.

news.headline: Bengals may get three players back from IR before PIT game
news.detail: Nov 12: Three Bengals players on injured reserve practiced fully and could be activated. The Bengals have scored 31+ points in each of four straight wins. Burrow's own status didn't come up in what I found.

news.headline: NE-DET in Munich: Henderson out, Stevenson and A.J. Brown questionable; Maye cleared
news.detail: Nov 13: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson, G Ben Brown and CB Carlton Davis are out. Drake Maye has no designation. Lions have three players out, and St. Brown (rib) was limited. Goff practiced fully with a chest listing.

NFL.recap: Week 9 went well on winners: 14 of 15 correct, with only GB-NE missed (NE had 4 turnovers). The spread was another story at 6-9, as the favorite covered in most games where the model had a smaller margin than Vegas. The Thursday game, WAS-NYG, went the other way: the model's winner was wrong by 5.1 points, but the spread and total both won. Over/under was 9-4 in Week 9 and 10-4 counting WAS-NYG.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has mostly lost so far.
lessons.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won. No Week 9 or WAS-NYG game disagreed with Vegas, so no new cases. HOU at CLE is this week's case (model CLE, Vegas HOU -4.5). The built-in past-season test says this does not hold up: the model's side won 43% in 2020-2025, about what Vegas's chances said.
lessons.test: Run the attached check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025: model's side to win when it differs from the Vegas favorite. Compare to Vegas's own chances. Wait for 20+ games this season.

test_result.note: Won 43% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 43%, about what Vegas's own chances said, so there's no edge.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: Before Week 9, 0 of 5 graded games with a gap of 4.9+ won the over/under pick; Week 9 split 1-1 (TB-CHI lost, CIN-ATL won). WAS-NYG (gap 2.7) won, JAX-BAL (4.2) won. Over/under is 30-24 overall. Built-in past-season test: model's side with a 4+ point gap won 48.3% in 2020-2025, which does not beat break-even. This week's L9 (Over 39.5, gap 5.3) fits this group.
lessons.test: Run the check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025: model's side of the total when the gap is 4+ points. Also compare groups under 2, 2-4 and over 4. Needs 20+ games this season.

test_result.note: Won 48.3% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: In 9 of the 16 games where the winner was wrong through Week 9, the review names efficiency as the main reason. The new miss, WAS-NYG, was close (5.1 points) with no named driver. BUF-MIN was off by 15.7, with efficiency worth about 10 points. Winners are now 39 of 56.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Long-shot picks (underdog winners and big-game props) hit a bit below the model's chances and lose units.
lessons.evidence: Underdog picks are 5 of 19 against 7.7 expected (-6.54 units). Big-game picks are 12 of 36 against 11.8 expected (-8.99 units). Big games hit right on expectation, so their loss is mostly from prices. The underdog gap is about 2.7 hits. Milestone picks are 31 of 40 against 29.9 expected (-3.29 units).
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for underdog winners and long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running a little below the model's chances.
lessons.evidence: 12 of 24 best-value picks hit this season, against 12.7 expected, at -1.09 units. The gap to expectation is under 1 hit now. This week's five value picks all sit only 0.4 to 1.0 points over break-even.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks per edge group.

lessons.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
lessons.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.7 for the model against 9.0 for Vegas over 56 graded games. The model is 25-31-1 against the spread. Winners are 39 of 56 (70%). Week 9 went 6-9 against the spread; WAS-NYG won.
lessons.test: Run the check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025: the model's spread side across all games. Also compare average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week and season, before changing anything.

test_result.note: Won 48.9% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas may come from lineup changes the model hasn't picked up.
lessons.evidence: 3 earlier cases: DAL at PHI and PHI at WAS (Hurts on IR) and MIN (Murray out, Wentz in). This week several games have new starters (BAL Brissett, ARI Beck, MIA McCord, SEA Lock, LV Mendoza, CLE Watson back). The brief lists them, so the model may already use them. BAL is the model's biggest edge, 8.3 vs Vegas 4.5. Still under 20 cases.
lessons.test: Run the check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025: model's spread side when a team starts a different QB than last game and the spread gap is 3+ points. Compare model margin error in those games with all others. Needs 20+ such games.

test_result.note: Won 54.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen short of the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: 16 of 24 most-likely-winner picks hit this season, against 17.4 expected, at -3.27 units. The shortfall is about 1.4 hits, down from about 2. Overall winners are 39 of 56 (70%).
lessons.test: Run the check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025: the model's side to win when its chance is 70%+ and it agrees with Vegas. Bucket by 70-79% and 80%+ and compare with the moneyline-implied chance. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

test_result.note: Won 78% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 77%, about what Vegas's own chances said, so there's no edge.

news.headline: Mississippi State still without QB Kamario Taylor against Auburn
news.detail: Taylor, out for the season with a toe injury, is one of six Bulldogs ruled out (Nov 12 report). Auburn has only one player out and is nearly healthy. This favors Vegas's side (Auburn) over the model's Mississippi State by 0.1.

news.headline: NC State badly banged up and under an interim coach vs Syracuse
news.detail: NC State has about seven former starters out, including LB Popo Aguirre, and is coming off a 41-3 loss to Duke under interim coach Todd Goebbel after Dave Doeren was fired (Nov 12-13). Syracuse also has OL injuries. This leans toward Vegas's side (Syracuse) over the model's NC State.

news.headline: Wake Forest QB Gio Lopez expected back at SMU
news.detail: Lopez missed the Merrimack game with a lower-body injury but is listed as probable and expected to start (Nov 10-12). That removes the main worry for the model's side (Wake Forest). One preview lists the moneyline near even, so Vegas sees this as close.

news.headline: Temple QB Ajani Sheppard expected back vs UAB
news.detail: Coach K.C. Keeler thinks Sheppard (foot) will play after he sat out the Navy game (Nov 9). His dual-threat running is a plus for Temple, which Vegas favors by 2.5. The model has UAB by 4.5, so the QB return leans toward Vegas's side.

news.headline: UCF missing RB Duke Watson and three DBs against Arizona State
news.detail: Watson (foot) is out, as are DBs DJ Bell, Demari Henderson and Kahmel Johnson, and UCF has about 15 players on its report against 6 for Arizona State (Nov 11-13). QB Alonza Barnett only just returned from a six-game absence. This helps the model's side (Arizona State) against Vegas's UCF -3.

news.headline: Ole Miss QB Chambliss cleared, but 11 Rebels out including RB Kewan Lacy
news.detail: Chambliss was probable Wednesday and came off the SEC report Thursday, so he should start (Nov 12). RB Kewan Lacy, OL Patrick Kutas and LB Keaton Thomas are out, and RB Makhi Frazier is questionable. Oklahoma has five out. Mixed for the model's Ole Miss side.

news.headline: Both App State and Marshall short on the offensive line
news.detail: Marshall LT Tariq Montgomery is out and DE Braydin Ward is questionable. App State has three starting linemen hurt and has lost two straight (Nov 11-12). Nothing clearly favors either side of this model-vs-Vegas split.

news.headline: Texas without LT Trevor Goosby (season) and has line and WR concerns at LSU
news.detail: Goosby was ruled out for the season after the Oct 24 Ole Miss win, and WR Cam Coleman has left two games early. Arch Manning was sacked six times against Mississippi State last week. A Texas Longhorns On SI headline on Nov 13 says several starters came off the first injury report, but I couldn't see details.

College.recap: Week 11 results shown (8 games) went well on winners and badly against the spread. The model picked 7 of 8 winners (only Ohio at Miami (OH) missed, where it also disagreed with Vegas), but it was 1-7 against the spread and 4-3 on totals. The favorite covered in 7 of 8, and the model was usually on the smaller-margin side (Louisiana, Memphis, Central Michigan, Western Michigan, Buffalo). Season record is 161 of 242 on winners, 112-124-4 against the spread, and 109-128 on totals.

lessons.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up, and the model's totals picks overall have lost more than they won.
lessons.evidence: Weeks 8-10: over hit in about 16 of 39 such games (41%). Season totals picks are now 109-128 (46%); the Week 11 results shown went 4-3 (Memphis, Ohio, Bowling Green, Western Michigan overs hit; Central Michigan, Buffalo, Toledo missed). Louisiana had no pick.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Also compare the model's and Vegas's average total error. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: Won 51.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes, but efficiency still leads.
lessons.evidence: Week 10, 26 of the 40 results shown missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 14, finishing drives 5, turnovers 4, nothing stood out 2, defensive/return touchdowns 1. Week 9 had efficiency first in 7 of 26; Week 8 in 15 of 25. Week 11 results had no reviews yet. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin, defensive/return touchdowns and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, this season has gone badly, but past seasons say the model's side holds up.
lessons.evidence: This season about 4 of 14 right (earlier 4 of 12; Week 11 added Ohio-Miami (OH), Miami (OH) won 34-17, and Week 10 had Western Kentucky-Middle Tennessee, Middle Tennessee won 51-42; both went to Vegas). Built-in test: the model's side won 47% in 2020-2025 against Vegas's 41%. Eight such games this week (Auburn, Syracuse, Wake Forest, UAB, Arkansas State, Arizona State, Ole Miss, App State), so mo…
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

test_result.note: Won 47% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 41%. Those chances have the bookmaker's cut removed; a real bet pays it, which eats a couple of points of that edge.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
lessons.evidence: Season: 12 of 30 hit against 15.3 expected, at -7.09 units. The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on all five picks this week. Two of this week's spread picks (San José State +12.5, Purdue +17.5) sit against the model's own margin (Air Force by 21.1, Iowa by 26.6), so the cover chances need checking.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Underdog picks have hit a bit less often than the model expected, but long prices have kept units positive.
lessons.evidence: Season: 10 of 29 hit against 11.5 expected, at +1.56 units. No new underdog results since last run. A few hits swing the units a lot, which shows how much luck is in this list.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: Season: 23 of 25 hit against 22.4 expected, at +0.49 units (was 22 of 24; 1 of 1 new). Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's over the season, and favorites have covered a lot lately.
lessons.evidence: Season (about 242 games): average spread miss 12.4 for the model against 11.8 for Vegas, a 0.6 gap. Winners right in 161 of 242 (66.5%), spread record 112-124-4. In the 8 Week 11 results shown the model was 1-7 against the spread and the Vegas favorite covered in 7 of 8.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, whether the gap changes by week of season, and whether favorites cover more often in November.

test_result.note: Won 50.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: When the model's margin for a favorite is 3+ points bigger than Vegas's, it has covered more often than not in the recent results, which clashes with the built-in test.
lessons.evidence: By my count in the Week 10-11 results shown, about 9 of 14 such games covered (Toledo, Liberty, Louisville, Jacksonville State, Boise State, North Texas, UAB, Wake Forest, Arizona State; Navy, Ohio State, Kansas, Mississippi State, Hawai'i did not). Under 20 games, and the built-in 2020-2025 test says the model's side on 3+ point gaps won only 49.0%. Seven games this week fit (Iowa, Liberty, Air…
lessons.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's margin for the favorite exceeds Vegas's by 3+ and check how often the favorite covers, split by size of spread and by week. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: Won 48.5% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.
